clue.text: Salad, shall we say?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: 'shall we?' is a suggestion that can be put as 'let us'

explanation.surface: Someone tentatively proposing a salad: shall we have one?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shall we' turns into the proposal 'let us', and 'say' tells you to speak those words, which give the sound of a salad leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: This leafy vegetable is the classic base of a green salad, so the salad stands for it.

clue.text: He won't get out quickly with one iron in both hands

indicators.note: in places the pair of pieces inside the outer one

parts.note: L and R, left and right, are both hands
I is one as a Roman numeral
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A man holding a golf iron in both hands won't be leaving in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one iron' looks like a golf club, but it is I plus FE between L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a life sentence is not going to be released soon.

clue.text: "God takes Perrier", he wrote

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
Perrier is a brand of mineral water, and eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A writer quotes a slogan claiming that a deity drinks Perrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Perrier stands for any French water: EAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau was an American writer, author of Walden.

clue.text: Natural waste product of pure alcohol

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: A waste product from the body is made from pure spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is the nitrogenous compound mammals excrete in urine, a natural waste.

clue.text: Other people's money gets laid out on them

definitions.text: Other people's money gets laid out on them

parts.words: Other people's money gets laid out on them
parts.note: these are records of expenditure charged to an employer, so the company's cash is spent through them

explanation.definitionFit: Business expense records let staff spend the firm's money, which is literally laid out on them.

clue.text: Native American complaint about symptom of drunkenness

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: a moan is a grumbling complaint
a hiccup, written HIC, is the cartoon sign of being drunk

explanation.surface: A Native American grumbling about someone showing signs of having drunk too much.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohicans were an Algonquian-speaking Native American people of the Hudson valley.

clue.text: Opera composer featuring wacky spirit board wanting one to be 12 in the 14 thus

parts.note: the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera

indicators.note: featuring means the composer's name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Thomas Arne was an English composer, writer of Rule, Britannia!
zany means wacky

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a Ouija board is used to contact spirits
I is one as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An eccentric composer uses a talking board at a seance to be introduced in the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is INTRODUCED and 14 is JUNGLE: the famous line of a jungle hero meeting the heroine. 'Opera composer' is two pieces, MET and ARNE.
explanation.definitionFit: The words are the legendary self-introduction from the Tarzan films, made deep in the jungle.

clue.text: Present tense first used in journal that gets handed down

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

indicators.note: used in means one letter is put into the following word

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A grammatical tense appears first in a journal passed down through a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present tense' looks like grammar, but 'Present' is HERE and 'tense first' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Traits or titles that pass from parent to child by inheritance are handed down.

clue.text: Youngster left diamonds outside booth

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a youngster

indicators.note: outside means the diamonds word goes around the letter

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A child leaves jewels outside a small booth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubicle is a small partitioned compartment, much like a booth.

clue.text: An aside about nymphs

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A whispered aside on the subject of nymphs.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads are water nymphs of Greek myth; this is the classical plural.

clue.text: Leading soldiers bolt back with piece of earthenware

indicators.note: back here turns the whole run of pieces round so it reads from the end

parts.note: top means leading, as in the top team
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of British soldiers
to bolt food is to wolf it down

explanation.surface: Front-line troops make a run for it, carrying a bit of pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolt' looks like running away but means eating fast (WOLF); 'back' reverses TOP, RE and WOLF together.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant container made of fired clay is a typical piece of earthenware pottery.

clue.text: Butler's AC/DC mentor

parts.note: R. A. 'Rab' Butler was a senior British Conservative politician of the 1950s
AC/DC is slang for bisexual, shortened to BI

explanation.surface: A man named Butler has a mentor who swings both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab Butler was a British Chancellor and Home Secretary; AC/DC (alternating or direct current) is slang for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher acts as a scholar and guide, so a mentor in the broad sense.

clue.text: King repelled charge on the rocks

parts.note: R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so this word is read in reverse

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A king fights off an attack while stranded on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' reads as an attack being repelled, but it is a payment, FEE, which is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of rock or coral just below the surface of the sea is a set of rocks.

clue.text: Brought in, making right deduction

indicators.note: making signals that the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A detective was brought in and made the correct inference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' asks you to make a new word from R plus the letters of DEDUCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something new or bring a person into company is to have brought it in.

clue.text: Wild, wild raves and gigs on Ecstasy

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the final letter after the rest
wild signals the letters are rearranged in a wild way

parts.note: E is the shorthand for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Raves and gigs where people are on drugs get wild.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Wild' is the definition, the second the signal to rearrange RAVES and GIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile and violent behaviour is aggressive, as is a wild, angry temper.

clue.text: Foreign article on explorer of the subconscious's untamed regions

indicators.note: on in an across clue lets the article follow the explorer's name

parts.note: Carl Jung was the Swiss psychiatrist who explored the unconscious mind
le is French for 'the', a foreign article

explanation.surface: A foreign piece about a psychoanalyst explores wild uncharted territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' is a grammar word, not a piece of writing: the French definite article LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense tropical forest is the archetype of wild land that nobody has tamed.

clue.text: Innocent as an empty gallery?

definitions.meaning: a gallery with no art in it would be lacking art, read playfully

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into ART plus -LESS: a gallery without any art.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without guile or cunning is being innocent; jokingly it also means having no art.

clue.text: Belt out incomplete bird call

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order
incomplete means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Sing loudly an unfinished birdsong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt out' looks like a single verb meaning sing loudly, but 'Belt' is the definition and 'out' the signal to rearrange BIRD with CAL (call less its last L).
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a belt worn over one shoulder across the body to carry a sword.

clue.text: To live with the wealthy is good

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
the haves are the rich, as in haves and have-nots

explanation.surface: Living among the rich is a fine thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who behaves acts properly, so they are being good.

clue.text: Woman's upper-crust origins in French city

indicators.note: in puts the picked letters inside the city name

parts.note: Lille is a city in northern France

indicators.note: origins picks the first letter of each part of the word

explanation.surface: A woman of aristocratic origins from a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucille is a woman's given name.

clue.text: The funny guy in Rocky I, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Asking whether the comic character in the first Rocky film is this one.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorick is the dead court jester whose skull Hamlet holds: 'a fellow of infinite jest'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hamlet the jester is remembered as a fellow of infinite jest, the play's funny man.

clue.text: Very important vineyard non-professional raised

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word reads upwards, in reverse

parts.note: laic means lay, not clerical or professional

explanation.surface: An amateur winemaker brought up a crucial vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crucial is decisive and of the greatest importance.

clue.text: Nefarious business, coppers standing in for models in hot spots

indicators.note: standing in means one thing takes another's place in the phrase
for, as in one thing for another, marks the second swap of the same kind

parts.note: taken as written: trouble spots or lively places
the Model T Ford makes T a crossword model; plural models means two of them
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; plural coppers means it happens twice

explanation.surface: Police officers replace fashion models in trouble spots in some shady dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing in for' covers both swaps: each T (Model T) in HOT SPOTS gives way to CU, the chemical symbol for copper, since the clue's plurals ask for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickery or deception meant to mislead is shady business, the sense of this conjuror's phrase.

clue.text: As dead as the heart of an Oxbridge college

definitions.text: the heart of an Oxbridge college

parts.note: qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', meaning as
D is the abbreviation for dead, as on genealogies

explanation.surface: Something at the centre of an old university college is lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: The quadrangle is the central courtyard round which many Oxford and Cambridge colleges are built.

clue.text: Discovered erect nipple?

parts.note: a dug is an udder or teat, so a nipple
up means upright, erect

explanation.surface: A risqué question about an aroused body part.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy surface hides an archaeological meaning: unearthed.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something by excavating it is to have discovered it.

clue.text: Move to secure accommodation

definitions.meaning: to move slightly or to set in motion
slang for prison, housing kept under lock

explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to move; stir is also slang for jail, very secure lodging.

clue.text: Gut linings required if sick in 6

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Lining of the gut needed if poorly with something inherited.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6-down but is just the Roman numeral VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Villi are tiny finger-like projections lining the small intestine.

clue.text: The immediate object is a close shave

definitions.meaning: the thing closest to hand, the nearest item
a narrow escape, something that only just failed to happen

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is the closest object; idiomatically it is a narrow escape.

clue.text: Kitchen utensils in Wesker's play

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are played with and moved about

parts.note: Arnold Wesker was a British playwright, author of The Kitchen

explanation.surface: Cooking tools that turn up in a drama by Arnold Wesker.
explanation.walkthrough: Wesker wrote a play called The Kitchen, which suits the surface; 'play' is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Long pointed metal or wooden pins for holding meat while it cooks are kitchen tools.

clue.text: Back from Scottish circuit with protective gear

indicators.note: Back tells you to read the word from end to start

parts.note: frae is the Scots form of from
a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: Returning from a Scottish race track with safety equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap on a hat that folds down to cover the ear protects it from cold.
